Dreck.et: From Middle High German drëc, from Old High German drec, from Proto-West Germanic *þraki. Cognate with Old Norse þrekkr and Swedish träck.

Dreckloch.et: From Dreck (“dirt, filth, shit”) + Loch (“hole, pit”).

s: swine, son of a bitch, bastard

Drechsler.et: From Middle High German dræhseler, from Old High German thrāhslāri; equivalent to drechseln (“to work a lathe”) + -er (“-er”).
From Middle High German dræhseler, from Old High German thrāhslāri; equivalent to drechseln (“to work a lathe”) + -er (“-er”).
